sources.//: This `exclude` list is the template engine's own default list MINUS `**/*.lock.json`, and it exists to keep that one pattern off (FS.GG.Templates#380). The default is not inert: it silently stripped every committed `packages.lock.json` out of each generated workspace, so the reviewed lock could never reach a product. Combined with `Directory.Build.props`'s `RestorePackagesWithLockFile=true`, the product's FIRST restore then AUTHORED its own lock from whatever the ambient host happened to resolve, and `RestoreLockedMode=true` enforced that unreviewed lock forever after — surfacing as `NU1403: Package content hash validation failed` the moment the ambient content moved. This template did not RED on #380 only because `build.sh` runs its npm steps before the locked restore and its solution has fewer restore passes to disagree across; the defect was identical. Declaring `exclude` here REPLACES the engine default wholesale, so every other default pattern below must be restated verbatim; they are copied from the engine's own defaults (dotnet SDK 10.0.302, Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Orchestrator.RunnableProjects). `**/node_modules/**` IS one of those defaults and this list dropped it — the restatement omitted it by silence, and this template is an npm workspace (`Web/`, `Web.Tests/`, `Browser.Tests/`), so the delivery leg went unguarded exactly where the engine used to guard it (FS.GG.Templates#386, measured: a package packed with `Web/node_modules/` present delivered it into the product); it is restored here. `**/.nuget/**` is the ONE pattern in this list that is NOT an engine default, and it is added deliberately (#386): the very `RestorePackagesPath` this template sets (#382) means the regeneration command this template's README documents materializes a workspace-local package folder INSIDE the template source — measured at 75M — and the engine, which knows nothing about that property, delivered it into every generated product. The four templates' lists are identical by intent; `tests/composition/lib/content-exclusions.sh` reds if any of them stops filtering either directory.

productName.description: Raw product name used in paths and display text. When omitted, --name supplies it.
